hints: Expand $\cos(\theta-60^\circ)$ using the cosine subtraction formula.
Substitute the exact values of $\cos60^\circ$ and $\sin60^\circ$, then divide by $\cos\theta$ to form an equation in $\tan\theta$.
Find the reference angle from the resulting positive tangent value.
Use the $180^\circ$ period of tangent to list every solution in $0^\circ\leq\theta\leq360^\circ$.
walkthrough:
Apply the compound angle formula $\cos(A - B) = \cos A \cos B + \sin A \sin B$ to expand the left-hand side of $\cos(\theta - 60^\circ) = 3\sin\theta$:
$$\cos\theta \cos 60^\circ + \sin\theta \sin 60^\circ = 3\sin\theta$$

Substitute the exact trigonometric values $\cos 60^\circ = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and $\sin 60^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$:
$$\dfrac{1}{2}\cos\theta + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\sin\theta = 3\sin\theta$$

Multiply the entire equation by $2$ to clear denominators:
$$\cos\theta + \sqrt{3}\sin\theta = 6\sin\theta$$

Group the sine terms on the right-hand side:
$$\cos\theta = 6\sin\theta - \sqrt{3}\sin\theta$$
$$\cos\theta = (6 - \sqrt{3})\sin\theta$$

Divide both sides by $\cos\theta$ and by $(6 - \sqrt{3})$ to express the equation in terms of $\tan\theta$:
$$\tan\theta = \dfrac{1}{6 - \sqrt{3}}$$

Rationalize the denominator by multiplying numerator and denominator by the conjugate $(6 + \sqrt{3})$:
$$\tan\theta = \dfrac{6 + \sqrt{3}}{(6 - \sqrt{3})(6 + \sqrt{3})} = \dfrac{6 + \sqrt{3}}{6^2 - (\sqrt{3})^2} = \dfrac{6 + \sqrt{3}}{36 - 3} = \dfrac{6 + \sqrt{3}}{33}$$

Find the basic acute angle in the first quadrant:
$$\theta_1 = \arctan(0.2343046) \approx 13.1867^\circ \approx 13.2^\circ$$

Add $180^\circ$ to find the corresponding third-quadrant angle within $0^\circ \leq \theta \leq 360^\circ$:
$$\theta_2 = 13.1867^\circ + 180^\circ = 193.1867^\circ \approx 193.2^\circ$$

State the two solutions correct to 1 decimal place:
$$\theta = 13.2^\circ \quad \text{or} \quad \theta = 193.2^\circ$$
